description: We are Team Orion. Inspired by the brightest constellation, we design an immersive web-based space simulation game. Our mission is to transform complex orbital mechanics, payload capacities, and resource management into an engaging gameplay experience. As Orion, we bring the discipline and wonder of space exploration into our code, crafting a strategically rich universe for players to master.
summary:
ASTROYARD is an interactive web-based aerospace engineering simulation where users step into the role of a Chief Engineer. Acting as a virtual spacecraft shipyard, the platform challenges users to select a space mission and design a functional spacecraft while balancing strict real-world constraints such as budget limits, mass, fuel efficiency, and orbital physics. By transforming complex rocket science and mission planning into an accessible, hands-on decision-making experience, ASTROYARD bridges the gap between theoretical aerospace engineering and public engagement. 
Our goal is to inspire students, educators, and space enthusiasts to think like real NASA mission planners. Instead of passively reading about space exploration, users experience the critical trade-offs behind every launch—understanding how budget, payload, and physics dictate mission success. Through interactive simulation, ASTROYARD fosters problem-solving skills, STEM curiosity, and a deeper appreciation for the engineering precision required in modern spaceflight.
details:
What does it do / how does it work?

ASTROYARD is an interactive web-based aerospace engineering simulation where users step into the role of a Chief Engineer. Acting as a virtual spacecraft shipyard, the application challenges users to select a space mission and assemble a functional spacecraft from various propulsion, structural, and payload components. The simulation calculates real-time physics parameters—including total mass, delta-V, thrust-to-weight ratio, and fuel efficiency—against strict mission budgets and orbital mechanics before executing a live launch sequence.

What benefits does it have?

ASTROYARD helps users—especially students, educators, and space enthusiasts—understand the real-world engineering trade-offs behind spaceflight. It transforms abstract rocket science formulas, mass ratios, and budget constraints into a tangible, hands-on decision-making experience. Users immediately see how changing a single component affects mission viability, fuel consumption, and cost.

Intended impact of the project:

Our goal is to make aerospace engineering accessible, intuitive, and engaging. By allowing users to test, fail, and iterate on spacecraft designs like real NASA mission planners, we aim to inspire curiosity about STEM, encourage systems-level thinking, and foster a deeper appreciation for the precision required in modern space exploration.

Tools, coding languages, and software used:

We built ASTROYARD using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create a responsive, lightweight web simulation. Orbital physics calculations, budget balancing, and interactive mission state logic were developed in vanilla JavaScript, and the project is hosted and version-controlled via GitHub and GitHub Pages.

Creativity and team considerations:

We focused on combining authentic orbital physics with an intuitive "Chief Engineer" narrative. Rather than presenting a static calculator or raw telemetry tables, we designed ASTROYARD as a clean, interactive mission control workspace that challenges users to solve open-ended engineering problems creatively within realistic financial and physical boundaries.
